Flow: Dana (donation) and merit-making. Stated purpose: Support monastics; generate merit. How it controls: Merit economics converts cosmology into revenue: giving buys better rebirth, refusal risks it. Who benefits: Monasteries, temples, monastic hierarchies ACADEMIC SOURCE.

Flow: Funeral and memorial services (Japan's danka system). Stated purpose: Care for the dead and ancestors. How it controls: The temples hold an effective monopoly, with very high fees for posthumous names (the Buddhist names given to the dead) and memorials, and families cannot easily exit.. Who benefits: Temple families and Buddhist sects ACADEMIC SOURCE.
Funeral and memorial services (Japan's danka system)

Flow: Retreat, course, and teacher-training fees (convert Buddhism). Stated purpose: Access to practice and training. How it controls: Paywalled advancement; unpaid work-exchange labor at retreat centers. Who benefits: Centers, senior teachers, certification pipelines.
Retreat, course, and teacher-training fees (convert Buddhism)

Flow: Mindfulness industry licensing and apps. Stated purpose: Secular wellbeing. How it controls: Technique extracted from its ethical framework and sold at scale with no accountability. Who benefits: Corporations, app companies, individual trainers.
Mindfulness industry licensing and apps

Flow: Amulets, blessings, merit-transfer rites. Stated purpose: Protection and blessing. How it controls: Micro-transactions on fear and hope; heaviest on the poor. Who benefits: Temples, monks, ritual vendors.
